neighbours.label: Singleness of extent: fires on the head of a phrase describing one unit or one dimension ('single|-element' list, 'straight| line' distance); multi-element collections, curved lines and 'line'/'element' in other senses stay quiet. The − pole is the explicit 'one dimensional' / 'on a line' / monochrome side
fire: The parser always wraps the value in a single-element list before returning it.
Measured as a straight line, the two towns are only six miles apart.
If the query matches one row, you get back a single-element array.
The crow flies in a straight line from the barn to the river.
The helper converts a scalar into a single-element vector for the solver.
Draw a straight line connecting the two dots on the page.
An empty result is different from a single-element set containing zero.
Light travels in a straight line unless something bends its path.
quiet: The parser always wraps the values in a nested dictionary before returning them.
Measured by road, the two towns are nearly forty miles apart.
If the query matches many rows, you get back a large array.
The crow circles above the barn and then lands by the river.
Carbon is the element that forms the backbone of organic molecules.
There was a long line of customers waiting outside the bakery.
An empty result is different from an error raised by the server.
The actor forgot his first line and the audience laughed.

notes: Card (max only 5.2): '-element' x3 (single-element), ' line' x2 (straight line), '1' x5, 'díg|ito' (um só dígito), ' projections', ' long'. Probes: 'single-element tuple' 0.72, 'straight line distance' 0.79, 'one digit' 0.22, '2.5 meters long' 0.10, unrelated 0.02-0.04. The shared pattern (one unit / one dimension) is a guess; the test only supports the two phrases.
